name: Jodensavanne Archaeological Site: Jodensavanne Settlement and Cassipora Creek Cemetery
description: Deep in the forest beside the Suriname River, about 50 km south of Paramaribo, lie the ruins of Jodensavanne, a Jewish settlement founded in the 1680s. Its crumbling synagogue is believed to be the earliest of architectural note in the Americas. Nearby are old graves, river landings and a military post, plus the older Cassipora Creek cemetery from the 1650s. The settlement's wealth was built on sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans.
